_experiment.description: Full resolution MNIST (28x28 = 784 inputs) vs the baseline 14x14 (196 inputs). The first layer grows from 196*10=1960 to 784*10=7840 weights, making the network 3.6x larger. The search step cost grows proportionally (more candidates per step). The question is whether the higher-dimensional input creates more or less redundancy: more input features means more potential zero-weight columns in L0, but the adjust step must now compensate over a 784-dimensional input domain. NOTE: requires full-resolution MNIST data files (X_train_full.csv etc.) — generate from raw MNIST if not present.
literature: LeCun et al. 1998 (MNIST): the standard 28x28 full-resolution benchmark — the thesis uses a downsampled version; this experiment validates results at standard resolution
Thesis sec:exp_setup: explicitly flags the 14x14 downsampling as a preprocessing choice — this experiment removes that choice
